entries.claim: The new at-risk predicate is dead code: the diff adds `censusesAtRisk()` but does not invoke it from the planning lease-check path (or any other enforcement path).
entries.failure_scenario: A plan declares `cadence-core/bin/lib/arg-contract.mjs` but omits `cadence-core/bin/arg-contract.test.mjs`. That edit can change the 184-entry census while leaving its assertion stale. `censusesAtRisk()` would identify the missing holder, but no changed production code calls it or turns its result into a refusal, so the plan is accepted and the stated census-protection goal is missed.

counter_evidence.note: Not dead code - a phase-split boundary the reviewer could not see, because its artifact was plan 1 s committed range alone. The uncalled predicate IS plan 1 s deliverable: PLAN-1.md under Must be true when done asks only that querying the registry be one call over the table. PLAN-2.md:109 is the task that wires it into cadence-core/bin/planning/lease-check.mjs (PLAN-2.md:100), asking this exact export which registered censuses a declared set puts at risk without declaring their holding file. The export exists at line 423 exactly as plan 1 specified.
